feat(routing): the policy comparison records the share the hard rules alone send to second review

feat(routing): fit the learned policy on val and compare it with the threshold policy

compare.py routes the test split with both policies through the same ReviewRouter and
providers, one decision log each, and writes policy_comparison.json and .md: modes, error
rate per mode, error catch rate, ice handling and routing time, with paired bootstrap 95%
intervals for the differences, under equal workload and equal catch rate (both chosen on
val). make compare-policies and compare-policies-cnn run fit + compare.

feat(routing): learned review policy, fitted on val, weights hashed into its version

Change scenario (b): replace the decision policy. LearnedPolicy (routing/learned.py) keeps the
hard safety rules, then a NumPy logistic regression on confidence, margin and agreement
predicts the risk that the primary model is wrong; two cutoffs chosen on val (equal
workload with the threshold policy) pick the mode. Registered as 'learned' in POLICIES;
the default policy stays threshold and --bundle-dir refuses any other. router.py, the
Protocols and log.py are unchanged.

feat(routing): margin provider, switched on by name in routing.extra_providers

Change scenario (a): a third confidence provider. MarginProvider is the gap between the
top-1 and top-2 temperature-scaled probabilities; run.PROVIDERS registers it so config can
enable it. router.py, the Protocols and log.py are unchanged.

Case/CaseView (providers and policies never see true_label), calibrated
confidence and model-agreement providers behind a ConfidenceProvider
protocol, ThresholdPolicy behind ReviewPolicy (light/full/second review, no
auto-accept), ReviewRouter with fallbacks that can only make review
stricter, and an append-only JSONL DecisionLog with outcome events.
Standard library and NumPy only.

feat(baseline): opt-in --save-probs for first-seed val/test probabilities

Adds roadcond.routing.probs, a plain-array .npz format for per-model class
probabilities (image ids, true labels, classes, seed), and lets the classical
baseline save predict_proba of each chosen first-seed model on val and test.
Off by default and requires --eval-test; baseline.json is unchanged.
